# Arabic Number Words

> Java library (Java 8+, no runtime dependencies) that converts numbers and money amounts into
> grammatically correct Arabic words (تفقيط / tafqeet). Handles integers up to 36 digits
> (|n| <= 10^36 - 1), decimals, negatives, masculine/feminine agreement, and the currencies of all
> 22 Arab League countries plus USD, EUR and GBP. All methods are static and thread-safe.

## Maven coordinates

- groupId: io.github.yazan-abuawwad
- artifactId: arabic-number-words
- version: 1.0.0
- Maven: <dependency><groupId>io.github.yazan-abuawwad</groupId><artifactId>arabic-number-words</artifactId><version>1.0.0</version></dependency>
- Gradle: implementation 'io.github.yazan-abuawwad:arabic-number-words:1.0.0'
- Package: io.github.yazanabuawwad.arabicwords
- Javadoc: https://javadoc.io/doc/io.github.yazan-abuawwad/arabic-number-words
- Source: https://github.com/Yazan-Abuawwad/Convert_Big_numbers_to_Arabic_words

## Public API

- ArabicNumberConverter (entry point, static methods):
  - toWords(long | BigInteger | BigDecimal | String [, Gender]): plain numbers; default gender is MASCULINE
  - toWords(long | BigInteger count, ArabicNoun noun): a count followed by a noun, with agreement
  - toCurrencyWords(BigDecimal | String | double amount [, ArabicCurrency]): money; default currency is JOD
  - toCurrencyWords(String amount, String isoCode): money in a built-in currency by ISO 4217 code
  - MAX_VALUE: 10^36 - 1
- ArabicCurrency: built-in constants JOD KWD BHD IQD LYD TND DZD SAR QAR OMR YER AED MAD EGP SDG LBP SYP
  MRU SOS DJF KMF USD EUR GBP; forCode(String); predefined(); of(code, unit, subunit, subunitsPerUnit)
- ArabicNoun.of(singular, dual, plural, accusative, Gender): a countable noun (plural for 3-10, accusative for 11-99)
- Gender: MASCULINE, FEMININE

## Key examples

All outputs below are produced by the library.

```java
import io.github.yazanabuawwad.arabicwords.*;

ArabicNumberConverter.toWords(1234);                    // ألف ومئتان وأربعة وثلاثون
ArabicNumberConverter.toWords(1234, Gender.FEMININE);   // ألف ومئتان وأربع وثلاثون
ArabicNumberConverter.toWords("1,250,000");             // مليون ومئتان وخمسون ألفًا
ArabicNumberConverter.toWords(new BigDecimal("12.05")); // اثنا عشر فاصلة صفر خمسة
ArabicNumberConverter.toWords(-15);                     // سالب خمسة عشر

ArabicNumberConverter.toCurrencyWords("1250.750");                      // ألف ومئتان وخمسون دينارًا وسبعمائة وخمسون فلسًا
ArabicNumberConverter.toCurrencyWords("100.25", ArabicCurrency.SAR);    // مائة ريال وخمس وعشرون هللةً
ArabicNumberConverter.toCurrencyWords("3.05", ArabicCurrency.SYP);      // ثلاث ليرات وخمسة قروش
ArabicNumberConverter.toCurrencyWords("5.008", "OMR");                  // خمسة ريالات وثماني بيسات

ArabicNoun book = ArabicNoun.of("كتاب", "كتابان", "كتب", "كتابًا", Gender.MASCULINE);
ArabicNumberConverter.toWords(2000, book);              // ألفا كتاب
```

## Behaviour notes

- Gender for money and counted nouns comes from the noun (e.g. ليرة and هللة are feminine); only plain numbers take a Gender argument.
- Money is rounded half-up to whole sub-units; 9.999 USD -> عشرة دولارات.
- String input accepts Arabic-Indic digits (١٢٣), the Arabic decimal mark (٫) and thousands separators (, ٬ _ space).
- Errors: out of range -> IllegalArgumentException; unparseable text -> NumberFormatException; unknown currency code -> IllegalArgumentException.
- The fraction of a plain decimal is read as one number after "فاصلة" (3.14159 -> ثلاثة فاصلة أربعة عشر ألفًا ومائة وتسعة وخمسون).
